acceptanceCriteria.criterion: **Given** the backend API server is running **When** the frontend application is initialized **Then** Next.js 14+ app directory structure is configured
**And** TypeScript is enabled with strict mode
**And** Tailwind CSS is installed and configured with dark mode support
**And** API client library is configured to connect to backend (axios or fetch wrapper)
**And** Environment variable configuration for API base URL (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL)
**And** Layout component includes responsive navigation structure
**And** Error boundary components handle runtime errors gracefully
**And** developers can run `pnpm run dev` and see a functional homepage at localhost:3000
**And** API calls to backend health endpoint succeed

artifact.title: Epic Technical Specification: Foundation & Infrastructure
artifact.snippet: - Next.js 15 with App Router (not Pages Router) - TypeScript strict mode - Tailwind CSS for styling with dark mode support - API client library connecting to Fastify backend - Responsive layout with navigation structure

artifact.title: Perrache - Epic Breakdown
artifact.snippet: As a frontend developer, I want Next.js application configured with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and API client setup, So that we have a modern, type-safe frontend foundation.

artifact.reason: Shared type for API health check response, ensuring type safety between frontend and backend.
Standardized error response format for all API calls.

constraint.description: The backend API server is configured to accept requests from 'http://localhost:3000'. The frontend application must run on this port for API calls to succeed.
The frontend must use the NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL environment variable to configure the backend API base URL.

tests.standards: The project uses Vitest for unit and integration tests and Playwright for end-to-end tests. The testing strategy follows a test pyramid approach, with a majority of tests being unit tests. Pre-commit hooks and a CI pipeline are used to ensure code quality.
tests.ideas: - Unit test the API client to ensure it correctly handles success and error responses. - Unit test the navigation component to ensure it renders correctly. - E2E test the homepage to verify that it loads and successfully calls the backend health check endpoint.
